metadata.title: Week 8 Summary: Empiric Antibiotic Treatment Groupings

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Hrishikesh. In Week eight, we analyze empiric antibiotic treatment groupings for Raman spectroscopy deep learning. While thirty-class bacterial isolate accuracy sits near eighty-two percent, clinical treatment group accuracy surges past ninety-six percent, matching the Nature Communications benchmark.

props.command: evaluate Raman bacterial classification: 30-class isolate vs. 8-class empiric antibiotic treatment accuracy.
props.runningText: mapping 30 reference isolates to 8 treatment groups...
output: ✓ 30 isolates mapped to 8 empiric antibiotic classes
✓ 80.5% of model misclassifications are clinically harmless

beats.narration_text: In severe infections and sepsis, clinicians cannot wait twenty-four to seventy-two hours for bacterial cultures. What matters clinically is not whether a strain is E. coli one or two, but whether the patient receives the correct first-line antimicrobial immediately.

props.text:
Hypothesis:
Isolate-level accuracy
is what matters clinically.
Wait: sepsis moves fast.
E. coli 1 vs E. coli 2
takes the same Meropenem.
Treatment groups measure
true clinical utility.

beats.narration_text: Evaluating three thousand unseen test spectra across thirty isolates shows the clinical leap. Legacy CNN jumps from eighty-two point two percent to ninety-six point five percent, while ResNet jumps from eighty point zero to ninety-four point eight percent, matching the published paper baseline.

How are thirty reference isolates partitioned into eight empiric treatment groups? Enteric rods receive Meropenem, Salmonella takes Ciprofloxacin, Pseudomonas takes Piperacillin-tazobactam, and Staphylococci take Vancomycin.

props.command: inspect ATCC_GROUPINGS: map 30 reference isolates into 8 clinical antimicrobial classes.
props.runningText: grouping reference pathogens by standard of care...
output: ✓ Vancomycin (7 Staphylococci: MSSA, MRSA, CoNS, 700 spectra)

beats.narration_text: In engine dot py, the ATCC groupings dictionary maps thirty reference isolate indices to eight antibiotic classes, enabling post-hoc evaluation during inference and direct eight-class heads with bootstrapped majority voting for patient samples.

props.code:
# 30 reference isolates mapped to 8 empiric antibiotic treatment groups
ATCC_GROUPINGS = {
    3: 0, 4: 0, 9: 0, 10: 0, 2: 0, 8: 0, 11: 0, 22: 0,  # Meropenem
    19: 1,                                               # Ciprofloxacin
    12: 2, 13: 2,                                        # TZP
    14: 3, 18: 3, 15: 3, 20: 3, 21: 3, 16: 3, 17: 3,     # Vancomycin
    23: 4, 24: 4,                                        # Ceftriaxone
    26: 5, 27: 5, 28: 5, 29: 5, 25: 5, 6: 5, 7: 5,       # Penicillin
    5: 6,                                                # Daptomycin
    0: 7, 1: 7                                           # Caspofungin
}

beats.narration_text: Breaking down accuracy across all eight antimicrobial groups reveals near-perfect separation for critical pathogens: Daptomycin achieves one hundred percent accuracy on Enterococcus faecium, while Caspofungin achieves ninety-nine point five percent on Candida yeasts.

When we inspect the error distribution, the clinical power of the model becomes clear: over eighty percent of all misclassifications occur within the same antibiotic treatment group, resulting in zero clinical penalty for the patient.

props.text:
Legacy CNN: 533 errors.
429 of them (80.5%)
are within the same drug group.
Only 104 true cross-group errors
out of 3,000 unseen spectra.
ResNet: 74% benign errors.
Spectral confusion is
clinically inconsequential.

beats.narration_text: Of the five hundred thirty-three isolate-level mistakes made by Legacy CNN, four hundred twenty-nine are benign within-group confusions like MSSA one versus MSSA two, leaving only one hundred and four cross-group errors across three thousand spectra.

During post-hoc testing, evaluate maps targets and predictions through ATCC groupings, computing exact isolate accuracy alongside clinical treatment accuracy in a single forward pass without re-training.

props.code:
# Post-hoc 30-to-8 treatment group evaluation
ab_targets = np.array([ATCC_GROUPINGS[int(t)] for t in all_targets])
ab_preds = np.array([ATCC_GROUPINGS[int(p)] for p in all_preds])
ab_correct = int((ab_preds == ab_targets).sum())
ab_acc = 100. * ab_correct / total

print(f'Isolate Acc: {acc:.2f}%, Treatment Acc: {ab_acc:.2f}%')
# Legacy CNN: 82.23% isolate -> 96.53% treatment group

beats.narration_text: For clinical deployment, ten-spectra majority voting simulates culture-free single-cell identification directly from patient biofluids, delivering ninety-nine percent accuracy in seconds. Try this evaluation on your spectroscopy models. Your turn.
